lanes.summary: The diff implements roots 1, 5, and the mutation-gate infrastructure (root 6) of PMAT-4621: chunked dense CUDA prefill bounded by a byte budget (dense_prefill_chunk_rows), new F16/IQ4_XS device dequant kernels wired into qwen35_dequant_f32 with bitwise CPU-parity tests, a correctness fix (graph_may_run) that stops the opt-in CUDA-graph replay path from corrupting KV on chunk 2+, and a new mutants-cuda CI shard + GATE-MUTANTS-CUDA-RULE that makes `gate` RED unless cuda-gated mutants deferred by the CPU section are measured by name-identical set on a real CUDA runner. Roots 2 (qk-norm forced serial) and 3 (chat KV 2048) are untouched, but this matches the ticket's own 50%/InProgress status and the roadmap entry committed in this same diff, which lists those as still-open acceptance criteria — a disclosed split, not silent scope-narrowing. Traced the chunk-loop's last_row indexing by hand: run_prefill early-returns on prefill_count==0 (existing guard, unchanged), so the new `(prefill_count - 1) % rows` cannot underflow, and dense_prefill_chunk_rows clamps rows>=1 so the modulo cannot divide by zero — the arithmetic is sound. The GATE-MUTANTS-CUDA-RULE bash block and its self-test table (scripts/check_ci_gate_mutants_cuda_rule.sh) correctly encode the AND-of-shas comparison and correctly treat an absent/empty not_measured output as "0" via the documented ${NM:-0} substitution. The two `#4621` fixup commits on top (fat_driver.py carrying `outputs` through emit_results_output; mutants_diff_gate.sh making --defer-unbuilt's directory before writing) are exactly what their commit subjects claim and are exercised by matching self-test rows added in the same diff.

findings.claim: dense_prefill_chunk_rows sizes the score-buffer budget using the full query head count (num_heads) rather than the GQA-grouped heads_per_kv (num_heads/num_kv_heads) that the pre-existing, unchanged attention_rows_for/chunk_rows_for pair in forward_qwen35_cuda_prefill.rs uses for the same kind of budget computation (that file's own doc comment says the score tensor is heads_per_kv × rows × L).
findings.fix: Non-blocking: heads_per_kv <= num_heads always, so this is more conservative (smaller chunks, more GPU launches) than strictly necessary under GQA, never incorrect or OOM-risking. If the dense (non-flash) qwen35 prefill genuinely computes per-query-head scores rather than per-kv-group scores, num_heads is the correct multiplier here and the two functions are not really duplicates; worth a one-line comment cross-referencing why this path differs from attention_rows_for, but not a defect.
